content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching, the eye most commonly symbolizes spiritual perception and the moral/spiritual condition of the inner person: the eye is the 'lamp of the body,' so that a 'healthy' or 'single' eye represents an enlightened, undivided, rightly-oriented heart, while a 'bad' or 'evil' eye represents inner darkness, moral corruption, or misdirected desire. The eye functions as the gateway or index of the soul—what and how one 'sees' reveals and shapes one's spiritual state.", "primary_basis": ["Matthew 6:22-23", "Luke 11:34-36", "Ephesians 1:18 ('the eyes of your heart enlightened')", "Psalm 119:18 ('open my eyes that I may see wondrous things')", "Matthew 13:15-16 (seeing eyes vs. blinded eyes as spiritual receptivity)", "John 9 (physical blindness/sight as a figure for spiritual blindness/sight)", "2 Corinthians 4:4 (the god of this world blinding minds/eyes)", "Revelation 3:18 (eye salve so that you may see)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Divine omniscience, watchfulness, and providential care: the 'eye(s) of the LORD' symbolize God's all-seeing knowledge and protective oversight of the world and his people.", "basis": ["Proverbs 15:3", "2 Chronicles 16:9", "Psalm 33:18", "Psalm 34:15", "Zechariah 4:10", "Hebrews 4:13", "1 Peter 3:12"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "The eye as the organ and symbol of desire, covetousness, and lust—the entry point of temptation and sin, sometimes demanding radical renunciation ('pluck it out').", "basis": ["1 John 2:16 ('the lust of the eyes')", "Matthew 5:28-29", "Genesis 3:6 ('a delight to the eyes')", "2 Peter 2:14 ('eyes full of adultery')", "Job 31:1 ('a covenant with my eyes')"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "The Semitic-idiom reading of Matthew 6:22-23 favored by many modern scholars: the 'good/single eye' means generosity and the 'evil eye' means stinginess, greed, or envy, connecting the saying to the surrounding teaching on treasure and mammon.", "basis": ["Matthew 6:22-23 read with Matthew 6:19-24", "Matthew 20:15 ('is your eye evil because I am good?')", "Proverbs 22:9 ('a bountiful/good eye')", "Proverbs 23:6 and 28:22 ('evil eye' as stingy person)", "Deuteronomy 15:9"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Affection, favor, and preciousness: 'the apple of his eye' as a symbol of God's cherished, protected people.", "basis": ["Deuteronomy 32:10", "Psalm 17:8", "Zechariah 2:8"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "In apocalyptic visions, multiplied eyes (on living creatures, wheels, the Lamb, or horns) symbolize fullness of knowledge, vigilance, and the Spirit's all-seeing presence.", "basis": ["Ezekiel 1:18", "Ezekiel 10:12", "Revelation 4:6-8", "Revelation 5:6 (the Lamb's seven eyes as the seven spirits of God)", "Zechariah 3:9; 4:10"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "The eye is a highly polyvalent biblical symbol, but there is a recognizable dominant strand centered on Matthew 6:22-23/Luke 11:34-36: the eye as the lamp of the body signifying spiritual perception and the inner moral condition. This dominant reading itself has an internal scholarly debate (moral/spiritual illumination vs. the Semitic generosity/stinginess idiom), which is noted as a distinct common alternative. The 'eye(s) of the LORD' as omniscience/providence is nearly as well established but applies to God's eye rather than the human eye, so context determines which sense is primary. Related idioms (eye for an eye as retributive justice, eye of the needle, log/speck in the eye) are proverbial usages rather than core symbolic meanings and were not listed as separate readings."}
